comments.author: @Graybeard_
comments.text: Crazy that I went down a very similar rabbit hole last week. Basically my prompt was to ask Gemini (2.5 Flash) if I had $10,000, would it guide me to increase that amount by 20% in one month. The result was paragraphs of warnings about how AI should not be used as an investment tool followed by pages of the historical averages of the stock market. I then asked about buying new or used items and reselling them for a profit. Gemini was immediately excited ("That is a fantastic idea!") lol and began listing all the different ways to buy low and sell high. It seemed to prefer buying/selling used items. I could be reading a lot into it, but it seemed that Gemini did not feel constrained by assisting in identifying ways to buy and sell new/used items.

comments.text: Interesting video. If AI can run businesses effectively, of course employees will be displaced. But, business operators are generally risk managers so the adoption curve will likely be some form of extreme S curve where little happens until there is enough conviction on the part of business owners that they can use AI for this purpose before it is suddenly very commonly used. Then, very rapidly, I see many businesses as we know them undergoing profound shifts as employees are shed, wealth is concentrated further until governments have little choice but to regulate AI companies in some way so as to protect tax revenue. The degree to which this happens will vary by country depending on how responsive they have to be to voters to maintain power.
